items.title: Game Boy Advance timing: the cartridge prefetch buffer and exact wait states
items.notes: Today a simple prefetch model. Measure with the jsmolka/AGS-style timing tests and mGBA's suite (mgba-suite) before and after; some demanding games depend on it.
items.result: Done 25 October (commits c7e2bb1, 7061656). Measured with Alyosha's timing tests (alyosha-tas/gba-tests, MIT, 133 ROMs written against a real console; mGBA's suite needs devkitARM, which this sandbox cannot download). Before: 47 of 133 (prefetch 1 of 18). After: 64 of 133, all 18 prefetch-buffer tests and both prefetch on/off tests; pinned in tests/gba.rs alyosha_timing_tests, fetched by scripts/fetch-test-roms.sh. What changed: the Advance CPU has its real two-opcode pipeline (each instruction's read at r15, jumps refill N then S); every access is sequential or not as the CPU says (N after any data or internal cycle); the prefetch buffer is modelled halfword by halfword the way the tests' author's own emulator (GBAHawk) does it; DMA: first unit N, rest S, internal cycles split before/after, an immediate DMA starts 2 cycles after its write and overlaps the CPU's internal cycles; the work RAM wait register ($04000800); timers on the shared prescaler with the real start delay (and the FFFF-on-enable overflow); registers read/written at the end of the access; ARM jumps keep bit 1. Reference used: GBAHawk (Alyosha's emulator) built locally in .scratch only, with a stand-in BIOS, as a cycle-by-cycle comparison (it passes 102 of 133 that way); nothing of it is in the repo. Older Advance save states still load (the new timing state is appended after the fixed layout). Speed: about 5% slower than before on the six homebrew games here. Not done (not prefetch or wait states): a DMA interrupted by a higher-priority one, interrupt entry delay, the serial port's timing, sprite fetch timing, BIOS-dependent start-up tests.

items.title: Sound accuracy: SameSuite's APU tests
items.notes: STATUS: SameSuite's APU tests mostly fail; normal game sound is fine. Follow SameBoy's APU model.
items.result: Done 25 October. cBoy's sound chip rewritten to run at its own 2 MHz clock the way SameBoy models it (behaviour followed, code written from scratch): countdowns that reload a tick late, trigger delays, envelope clocks that lock, zombie-mode volume nudges, the sweep's delayed recalculation and its NR10 glitches, the noise channel's 14-bit counter and its NR43 write glitches, the DIV event on the falling edge and the envelope set-up on the rising edge, wave memory access while playing, revision E of the Color (the Game Boy's own differences where known; the Advance's PSG uses it too). SameSuite's 70 sound tests: 9 -> 57. SameBoy itself, built here from source and run on the same files, passes exactly the same 57 and fails the other 13 with byte-identical results (7 are for other revisions, 6 SameBoy also gets wrong). Blargg's dmg_sound and cgb_sound: 17 -> 24 of 24. Both pinned in tests/roms.rs (blargg_sound, samesuite_sound); scripts/fetch-test-roms.sh fetches Blargg's and builds SameSuite with rgbds. Older save states still load (the chip is saved after the fixed layout; an old state's channels carry over). Speed: within a few percent of before.

items.result: Done 25 October. New cBoy settings: 'Let games see a newer console' (System; Off / Pocket and Super Game Boy 2 / Advance (Color games) / Both; with the console on Auto a Game Boy game gets a Pocket, a Super Game Boy one a Super Game Boy 2, a Color one an Advance; default Off); Game Boy palette 'Automatic (Pocket colours on a Pocket)'; 'Super Game Boy speed' (Real, a little fast, default / Same as a Game Boy; the Super Game Boy 2 now runs at a Game Boy's speed, as the real one has its own clock); 'Game Boy Player reset' (Off default; on the Advance console a reset fades out over 35 frames and holds dark and silent for 94, as speedrunners measured the real Player and GSE does); 'Skip waiting loops (Game Boy and Color)' (Performance, Off default): exact, a loop that reads only memory nothing but the CPU's writes changes is clocked through without running the CPU and handed back at the exact point an interrupt would be taken; checked identical over 600 frames of test loops and 6000 frames of Pokemon Red and Crystal (built from pret here); it saves about 9% while a game busy-waits, nothing for games that use HALT (Pokemon does), so it stays off by default. Fast SGB transfers: nothing to add, cBoy's Super Game Boy starts the game at once. The network-link rows are now n/a (the app links phones). Inventory regenerated: libretro gaps 22 -> 8, all of them the two-consoles-on-one-phone link (B7) and the Advance link (B8); standalone gaps left: camera (B6) and the second player's save (B7).

items.notes: Why this one is next: Continuum already has its own Z80 (cores/continuum-arcade/src/z80.rs) passing SingleStepTests' Z80 suite, ZEXDOC and ZEXALL. The rest: the VDP (TMS9918 modes plus Mode 4, Game Gear palette and window), the SN76489 sound chip, the YM2413 FM chip (Japanese Master System), the Sega, Codemasters and Korean mappers, the Game Gear start button and link, light phaser and paddle. The bar: Gearsystem (the app's current core) and Genesis Plus GX; settings = every setting Gearsystem, Genesis Plus GX, PicoDrive, SMS Plus GX and Emulicious offer, plus our own (do a settings inventory first, like cBoy's and the GameCube's). Tests: ZEXALL for the Z80 on the real memory map, the SMS VDP test ROMs (Flubba's VDPTEST, the SMS Test Suite), and real open-licence homebrew. Replaces Gearsystem (GPL v3) when it matches it.
